payload.reason: The evidence provides a clear description of the crowdsourcing scheme used to instruct workers on identifying important elements in document collections.

claims.text: Crowd workers were instructed to identify important elements by scoring propositions based on their importance in a document cluster, using only a description of the topic and the propositions without reading the documents.

The crowdsourcing scheme, called low-context importance annotation, allows workers to make quick and simple decisions about importance without needing to read all documents, thus improving efficiency and scalability.
Workers used a 5-point Likert scale for more nuanced importance annotations, rather than binary decisions, enhancing the quality of the annotations.
